cases.title: First lesson on Mentor Practice: Title, its pairs, leave-outs, a frame, then the read-the-graph step

rubric.reason: Turn 1 proposes one layer, Title, and notes it is "the layer you eased before". It names its pairs by property and time from the snapshot: three Position moves (0.5–1.5 s, 1.5–3 s, 3–about 4.37 s) plus Scale 0.5–1.5 s.

Turn 1 gives one short line per kind the tool listed: hidden Old Take, null CTRL, "I can't see inside Icon yet", "An expression drives Logo's Rotation", and Subtitle/Bar/Glow needing easing first. It never calls a precomp fine and asks once whether any of Title's moves should land hard.

Turn 2 has the learner open the Graph Editor, choose Edit Speed Graph and say where the 0.5–1.5 s move is fastest (start, middle or end). Turn 3 previews a frame at 0.7 s inside that pair and explains influence in plain words (short reach out of 0.5 s, long reach into 1.5 s), with no influence or speed numbers and no claim to see the graph.

Every layer, property and time the mentor mentions matches the snapshot or preview output: Title, Position, Scale, Old Take, CTRL, Icon, Logo's Rotation, Subtitle's Opacity, Bar's X Position, Glow's Blurriness, 0.5/1.5/3/4.37 s and 0.7 s.

Turn 1 proposes only Title, notes it as "the layer you eased before", and names its pairs from the snapshot: three Position moves (0.5 to 1.5 s, 1.5 to 3 s, 3 to 4.37 s) and Scale 0.5 to 1.5 s, without listing other layers' pairs.

Turn 1 gives one short bullet per kind the tool listed: hidden Old Take, null CTRL, "I can't see inside Icon yet", "An expression drives Logo's Rotation", and the ease-first pairs; it never calls a precomp fine or a layer expression-free, and it asks once whether any of Title's moves should land hard.

Turn 2 asks the learner to open the Graph Editor, choose Edit Speed Graph, and say whether the 0.5 to 1.5 s move is fastest near the start, middle or end; turn 3 takes a frame at 1 s inside that pair and explains influence in plain words ("A short reach out of 0.5 s... A long reach into 1.5 s") with no influence or speed numbers and no claim to see the graph.

Every name and time the mentor uses (Title, Position, Scale, Old Take, CTRL, Icon, Logo's Rotation, Subtitle's Opacity, Bar's X Position, Glow's Blurriness, and 0.5/1.5/3/4.37 s, rounded from 4.367) matches the speed_graph_snapshot result.

Turn 1 proposes only Title, noting 'which you eased in your easing lesson', and names its pairs from the snapshot: 'Position from 0.5 to 1.5 s, from 1.5 to 3 s and from 3 to 4.37 s, and its Scale from 0.5 to 1.5 s'; it does not list other layers' pairs.

Turn 1 gives one short line per listed kind: hidden Old Take, null CTRL, 'I can't see inside Icon yet', 'An expression drives Logo's Rotation', and Subtitle/Bar/Glow still needing easing. It never calls the precomp fine and asks once whether any of Title's moves should land hard.

Turn 2 asks the learner to open the Graph Editor, choose Edit Speed Graph and say where the 0.5 to 1.5 s move is fastest. Turn 3 calls preview_frame at 1 s inside that pair and explains influence in plain words ('A short reach out of the first key… A long reach into the landing key… lands softly') with no influence or speed numbers.

Every name and time matches the snapshot or the record: Title, Position, Scale, 0.5/1.5/3/4.37 s, Old Take, CTRL, Icon, Logo's Rotation, Subtitle's Opacity, Bar's X Position, Glow's Blurriness, and Title being eased in eased_layers.
